messages:
mia: getting paged — apiserver 5xx spike in eu-west1, controller-manager flapping and a big GPU autoscale. graphs show fd usage on proxies climbing steadily. looks like a socket leak in the proxy multiplex layer.

sre-bot: [ALERT] apiserver: 503 rate exceeded (eu-west1) — 3270012345 — severity: high

aj: copying logs / what do you see on node-level? any CLOSE_WAITs?

mia: pulling a couple outputs now. short lsof from one proxy node: 
```
root@node-12:~# lsof -p 2345 | wc -l
65542
root@node-12:~# ss -tan state close-wait | awk '{print $5}' | sort | uniq -c | head
  12000 10.1.4.23:10250
   8000 10.2.1.8:32768
   3000 10.3.5.9:9000
```
roughly 65k fds for the proxy process (multiplexer PID 2345). many towards nodes' kubelets and our gpu-attach endpoint.

leo: that fd count is insane — likely leaking not closing after TLS termination. did we just push the new proxy multiplex changes earlier?

mia: we rolled the proxy multiplex change yesterday evening. rollout looked fine but traffic patterns shifted. regress?

kate: can we bisection-roll the proxy daemonset? or quick mitigation: restart proxy on a subset of nodes to drop sockets and see if apiserver errors reduce.

natalie: note: Dedicated GPU autoscaler kicked in at 03:11 and added 12 nodes — cost alarm already triggered. if this is caused by proxy leak we'll keep paying for scaleouts.

aj: agree do a partial rolling restart and watch fd counts + apiserver 5xx. I can run a safe drain+cordon script for 10 nodes.

mia: rolling restart started on 10 nodes: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/proxy -n kube-system --field-selector=spec.nodeName=node-1,node-3,...` (doing in small batches).

deploy-bot: infra-deploy: restarted daemonset/proxy on nodes [node-11,node-12,node-13] — 3270012352

leo: after restart node-12 fd count dropped to ~300, apiserver 5xx for that AZ decreased by ~70%. good signal.

mia: confirmed: apiserver 5xxs reduced cluster-wide from 1200/min to ~200/min after first 3 nodes restarted. controller-manager restarts reduced too.

kate: root cause hypothesis = proxy multiplex change not closing backend connections on TLS teardown under bursty long-lived streams (embedding/kv cache traffic to gpu-attach). need a repro. can someone capture packet traces on a repro node?

aj: grabbing tcpdump on node-13 for the gpu-attach port. also enabling `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` metrics.

natalie: pls also add a quick policy to prevent further autoscaler scaleups: set cluster autoscaler to scale-down-only for eu-west1 until we stabilize, otherwise costs blow past threshold.

mia: set CA to conservative: `kubectl patch configmap cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --type merge -p '{"data":{"maxNodeProvision": "0"}}'` — temporary.

leo: opened an issue for the proxy multiplex PR with logs and traces: https://infra/ops/PR-2698 — tagging networking and runtime.

mia: action items: 1) finish rolling restart across proxies (aj) 2) capture tcpdump + lsof+ss (aj) 3) run reproducer against staging with multiplex enabled (leo) 4) revert or patch proxy multiplex to close TLS backends on stream close (kate) 5) monitor autoscaler/costs (natalie).

aj: running reproducer now in staging — will post results.

sre-bot: [INFO] cost-alert: EU-WEST1 Dedicated GPU spend +18% vs baseline — triggered 3270012360

mia: thanks team. if restarts keep apiserver healthy we'll keep CA change for 4 hours then re-evaluate. posting snippet of suspected stack trace: 
```
E 03:09:12 proxy/mux.go:482: failed to close backend conn: timeout on write
W 03:09:12 proxy/mux.go:490: leaked stream session id=0x7f23...
```

kate: next-day work: add unit + integration tests for stream close path, and add FD metrics to proxy for early detection.

natalie: also flag finance to expect a bump on tonight's run if autoscaler didn't scale down. I'll keep alerts on. :money_with_wings:

mia: updating incident notes and will convert this thread to a formal postmortem if we end up reverting. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
